stem: Imran checks a flat card cut-out of six equal squares joined edge-to-edge in a straight row of four with one square attached above the second square and one square attached below the third square.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides whether this arrangement is a valid mathematical net for a cube?

options.text: It is a valid cube net: the six squares can fold without overlap into the six faces of a cube, and joining flaps are not counted as faces.
Accept it as a net just because it has six squares, even if those squares would overlap when folded.
Count a cardboard joining flap as a seventh face of the mathematical net.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A mathematical net must fold into the solid without face overlap; flaps used only for joining are not faces of the net. This hexomino folds to a cube.

teacher.key_rationale: The described hexomino is a known valid cube net. Counting six faces alone without foldability, or counting a joining flap as a face, both miss the net hinge.
